findings.title: Waking from sleep auto-rejoins a saved seat with no live session, which can discard a couch run or put an idle connection into another player's seat
findings.claim: owner.resume() calls dispatch({type:'reconnect'}) whenever a saved seat credential exists. It does not check whether an online session was live when the PC went to sleep. The saved seat is loaded from userData at every app start and survives Leave; only Forget clears it. Any user who ever played online therefore rejoins that room on every wake, unprompted. If the room is still active and the user is a guest, the guest connection gets set up and a port is published to the visible renderer. Receiving a port switches the app to online mode and disposes the couch session. In duel/flight mode (Helm) nothing receives the port. The host then swaps the seat's bot for an idle connection until the 30 s sync wait and retries run out.
findings.evidence: src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L544 (resume: `if (!disposed && saved && !operation && !disposal) await dispatch({ type: 'reconnect' })`, no context check); L551-L554 (saved seat loaded at startup); L483/L536 (leave -> prepareExit -> stop, `saved` kept); L425/L182/L202 (active guest: setupPeers -> onReady -> attach -> publish port); src/main/network/onlineIpc.ts:L53,L61 (powerMonitor resume -> owner.resume); src/main/network/onlinePlatform.ts:L50-L55 (port posted to the visible window); src/renderer/src/main.ts:L72 (`bridge?.onPort(... session.selectOnline().attach(...))`); src/renderer/src/app/sessionRouter.ts:L11 (selectOnline -> clear() disposes couch); src/renderer/src/main.ts:L101-L117 (duel/flight create no online bridge, but src/main/index.ts:L40-L52 still builds and registers the owner). Net-3 spec L23 ('resume remains paused until explicit player action'), L49 (Resume saved session is an explicit choice).
findings.why: Ordinary path: play online as a guest, press Leave (the room continues with a bot in your seat), start a couch game, sleep and wake the PC. The couch run is destroyed and the user is dropped into the old room. In Helm duel mode the other players' crew loses its bot to an idle connection. Nothing reproduces it in tests, because nothing ties resume to a session that was live before sleep.
findings.fix: Record at suspend whether a live or saved context existed (context?.seat and phase not idle/error). In resume(), only invalidate and reconnect in that case. Never reconnect from idle, or when no context existed. Separately, make the renderer's onPort handler refuse to switch out of couch/home mode. Close the port unless the user has already selected online mode.

findings.title: A TURN credential failure on one peer link tears down the host's whole authority; reconnect/re-host within 60 s of the last issuance cannot recover
findings.claim: onlinePeers routes any failure to get ICE credentials, before the attempt starts, to the session-level onFailure. On the host, onlineSession.fail() handles 'turn-unavailable' or 'rate-limited' with stop(code), which disposes the utility authority and closes the socket for every player. The 'unavailable' code takes the savedState path instead, which also retires the host. The ICE owner allows one fetch per 60 s, and the cache is cleared on every game retire or owner change. The Worker also limits each seat to one attempt per 60 s. So any seat that must re-link within 60 s of its previous fetch fails: a new host after a re-host, guests following it, or a guest whose link flapped. The retry loop gives up immediately when retryAfter goes past its 30 s window. Local recovery proofs use loopback ICE, which skips this code entirely.
findings.evidence: src/main/network/onlinePeers.ts:L118-L123 (acquisition failure -> retire + failed(error)); src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L184 (onFailure -> fail(c, codeOf(error))); L134 (allow-list excludes 'turn-unavailable'/'rate-limited'); L144 (`else void stop(code)`); L158 (retireGame -> c.ice.invalidate); L179 (`c.ice ??=` reused across re-host); L382-L383 (re-host winner sets up peers with the same ice); src/main/network/onlineIce.ts:L21 (invalidate keeps nextRequest), L42-L44 (local 60 s throttle); services/signalling/src/turn.ts:L105-L107 (per-seat 60 s 'rate-limited'); src/main/network/onlineRetry.ts:L29-L30 (`at >= end` -> retry-exhausted); onlineIce.ts:L37 (loopback bypass). Net-3e spec L80 ('Treat provider failure as an explicit retryable connection failure'), L84.
findings.why: Repro (HTTPS/TURN config): guest B's link drops and reconnects, fetching credentials at time T. The host dies at T+5 s. After lease expiry B presses Re-host at about T+25 s. B's new authority restores and the peers reconcile. The first link's ice.get throws rate-limited and fail() runs stop('rate-limited'), destroying the just-restored authority and dropping every guest. Surviving guests that fetched within the last minute fail to follow the new host the same way. A transient provider failure or the daily cap hit by one guest's re-link after about 55 min (cached credentials near expiry) also ends the game for everyone.
findings.fix: On the host, scope credential failures to the peer. Block that seat for retryAfter and schedule reconcile() then, not onFailure. Keep the session-level failure only for guests. Let the Worker re-bind the seat's still-valid issued batch to the new authenticated connection/generation instead of returning rate-limited (no extra provider calls or quota). Or let the retry loop schedule a delayed retry when retryAfter exceeds the 30 s window, instead of retry-exhausted. Add a native or unit recovery test with iceMode 'turn' and a fake provider.

findings.title: One failed mirror adopt stops all later automatic checkpoint deliveries for the session
findings.claim: The utility pushes one checkpoint candidate at a time and keeps later ones only as a single replacement until main acknowledges the current one. Main acknowledges only after mirrors.adopt() succeeds. If adopt rejects (for example, a candidate over 256 KiB fails validation, or the GET reconciliation fails on a reset mirror), the candidate is never acknowledged and nothing times out or retries. Every later periodic, pause or safe-point capture becomes the stored replacement and is never delivered. The DO checkpoint stops advancing even after captures become valid again.
findings.evidence: src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L258-L261 (ack only in adopt().then; the catch only rejects the initial capture); src/network/utilityHost.ts:L29-L30 (`if (!unacknowledged) deliver(value); else ... replacement = value`), L106-L112 (delivery advances only on ack); src/main/network/onlineMirrors.ts:L121-L130 (adopt throws on validate/refresh failure). Net-3e spec L54 ('If a boundary is not serializable, keep the previous valid checkpoint and retry at the next valid completed boundary').
findings.why: Abrupt host loss then rolls back to the last checkpoint before the failure, possibly far behind. The status still looks committed, so the loss is not obvious.
findings.fix: Have main acknowledge (or explicitly reject) every candidate it handled, success or failure, so the utility delivers the next one. Alternatively, keep the most recent candidate as a replacement in the utility and resend it after a short timeout. Add a test where one oversized candidate is followed by valid ones.

findings.title: Lease, ticket and link expiries depend on the local wall clock; a host whose clock runs fast gets fenced periodically or cannot start
findings.claim: Server deadlines use server Date.now(): leases expire 15 s after renewal, socket tickets and links after 30 s. The client compares them with its own Date.now(), with no offset correction. With the host clock S seconds fast, the utility deadline is min(start+12 s, 15−S−RTT s). For S ≳ 10 s permission lapses before the next 5 s renewal, so settleFence pauses the game ('session-fenced') each cycle and a manual Resume is needed. For S ≥ 15 s startup always fails with lease-expired. For S ≥ 30 s socket tickets and link-issued events are judged already expired and the connection fails.
findings.why: Standalone Windows PCs sync their clocks infrequently, so several seconds of drift is plausible. The result is unexplained pauses or failed starts with no actionable error.
findings.fix: Return a server-now or remaining-ms value with grants, tickets and link issuance. Turn it into a local monotonic deadline anchored at the request start, keeping the 12 s cap and the 'already expired' check relative to server time. Or estimate the offset from the HTTP Date header or the handshake.

findings.title: Suspend retires the host without the trusted pause and best-effort save; suspending while idle shows status error 'suspended'
findings.claim: owner.suspend() invalidates the lease and calls savedState(), which disposes the authority immediately. It does not request a pause or 'exit' capture first. Suspending with no seat calls stop('suspended'), so the status becomes phase 'error' even when the user was never online.
findings.evidence: src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L543; L119 (stop(reason) -> phase 'error'); Net-3 spec L23 ('Suspend requests a trusted pause and best-effort save').
findings.why: Up to one checkpoint interval (300 ticks) of host progress is lost on every sleep, and idle users see a spurious error.
findings.fix: In suspend(), bound a graceful(c)-style pause plus exit capture (and mirror persist) before retiring. Leave idle status unchanged when there is no context.

verified: Lease gate: one current nonce; the grant deadline is min(request-start + 12 s, server expiry); stale or reordered replies are rejected; expiry keeps a newer in-flight request (leaseGate.ts:L37-L42, L56-L59, L74-L89).

Utility owns permission: identity is checked on initialize; grant/invalidate/bootstrap requests are stamped and validated; a fence is forced when expiry happens inside accept (utilityHost.ts:L82-L95, L128-L157).
The authority core checks permission before admission, controls and each catch-up tick; beforeTick returning false stops the tick driver itself (core.ts:L213-L224, L472-L477; tickDriver.ts:L37-L44).

A fence rejects pending work, neutralizes held input and records a lifecycle pause; regrant resets the paused epoch with no debt; player Resume is rejected while closed (core.ts:L200-L212, L222, L488, L326-L330; tickDriver.ts:L60-L66).
Replay v4 is used only for fenced control prefixes and discarded lifecycle Resumes; the parser rejects v4-only fields in v2/v3 (core.ts:L181-L184, L400-L405; authority/replay.ts:L53-L55).
Periodic capture reuses the completed 300-tick baseline and refuses pending, in-flight or queued player controls (core.ts:L100-L121, L441-L444).
Initial Start waits for the initial capture, the utility-originated grant and a DO-committed flush before completeBootstrap (onlineSession.ts:L263-L272).
Re-host validates the service checkpoint before and after the claim, adopts the generation from host-changed rather than guessing, and the loser follows the winner (onlineSession.ts:L347-L383).
The DO checkpoint PUT requires an active lease, a matching generation and a monotonic (generation, sequence); an identical sequence must be byte-identical (checkpoints.ts:L29-L73).

The mirror store has a bounded 544 KiB binary container with exclusive temp file, sync and rename, and strict decode; Forget queues clears after cancellation (mirrorStore.ts:L22-L94; onlineSession.ts:L484-L493).
Named IPC checks the sender and frame, and status copies are validated so tokens never reach the renderer (onlineIpc.ts:L21-L35; serviceClient.ts:L413, L442).

Service client: tokens are sent only in Authorization headers or the first socket message, never in URLs; host-changed and claim replies are validated against generation + 1 (serviceClient.ts:L181-L198, L219-L225, L496-L497).
HTTPS config survives the re-resolution in createOnlineSession (onlineConfig.ts:L4-L15; onlineSession.ts:L47-L48).
